correctness.rationale: The normalized nearest-neighbor energy has nonconstant eigenvalues 1 and 1+q with q=(1+sqrt(5))/2. Write u=(1+v+w)/sqrt(1+s), s=r²+b², where v,w are the first and second real harmonics of norms r,b. Normalized Taylor expansion gives deficit 2q b²-2<v²w>+3r⁴/4+o(b²+r⁴); the quartic terms in first harmonics are s²/2 and <v⁴>/6, with <v⁴>=3r⁴/2 and <v³>=0. The mixed terms are uniformly lower order on the stated error scale, e.g. r³b<=r(r⁴+b²)/2. If b/r² diverges, b² dominates both the other numerator terms and (r²+b²)². Otherwise d(u)^4 equals r⁴(1+o(1)); completing the square subtracts ||P₂(v²)||²/(2q)=r⁴/(4q). The normalized path w=P₂(v²)/(2q) achieves the lower limit, giving (7-sqrt(5))/8. I independently recomputed the witness from integer successive differences and rational enclosures of the logs (a range-reduced series for -log(1-t), rather than the frozen atanh series). The certified ratio lies between 0.594923412098787 and 0.594923412098788, below 119/200 and the exact local threshold. The local separation excludes an entire ball about 1 at any level at or below the witness. Continuity including zero coordinates and compactness on the remaining closed set imply attainment and uniform positive separation of the minimizing set.
residual_risks: The witness is an upper bound, not a certified optimizer. The exact global constant, symmetry, and classification of all minimizers are unresolved.
